objective: In claude.ai cloud sessions only, make holyagent commits use the user as author (taken from the GitHub connector, never stored in repository files) while keeping the cloud's Claude committer, so branch commits are Verified; outside claude.ai keep the machine identity unchanged.
scope: Facts (probed 2026-10-27 in this cloud session): CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=cloud_default are set; /root/.gitconfig has user.name Claude, user.email noreply@anthropic.com, commit.gpgsign true, gpg.format ssh via /tmp/code-sign. A commit with author David Basile Filho <davidbasilefilho@gmail.com> and committer Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> showed verification valid on GitHub; author and committer both the user gave unknown_key. mcp__github__get_me returns login davidbasilefilho, id 39467981, name David Basile Filho, no email.

Design: (1) git's author.name and author.email config keys set the author without touching the committer; in the cloud the root sets them in the clone's local config (.git/config, not a repository file) from get_me: name = details.name, email = <id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com. Offer a CLI command, e.g. `holyagent vcs identity --name <n> --email <e>`, that writes exactly those two local keys, so the root does not hand-edit git config. (2) vcs commit: when CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true, require an author (author.* or GIT_AUTHOR_*) that does not look like an agent, and allow the Claude committer; otherwise keep today's check of user.name/user.email. Its error hint in the cloud names the get_me + identity command steps. (3) Move the identity guidance out of the static root text (packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/root/version-control.md Identity bullet, requirements.md R-VCS identity clause, requirements/commit-text.md:5) into the session-start hook context, emitted only when CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true (packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts, sessioncontext.ts; respect CONTEXT_BUDGET). Locally the static text says: commits use the configured git identity. (4) The no-agent-attribution rule covers the author and the commit text; the cloud committer is the documented exception.

Tests: cloud and non-cloud vcs commit identity cases, the identity command, the session-start context with and without CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE. Update docs/commit-authorship.md and docs/usage.md accordingly.

notes:
- **Design choice:** in the cloud, `vcs commit` takes the author from `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT`. That is git's own resolution (`GIT_AUTHOR_*`, then `author.*`, then `user.*`), so a missing author and an agent-looking one both fail with the new `CloudAuthor` error (exit 3). Its hint names the `get_me` and `vcs identity` steps. Locally the old `AgentIdentity` check and hint are untouched.
- **`vcs identity --name <n> --email <e>`:** it writes only `author.name` and `author.email` with `git config --local`. It refuses agent-looking values, a malformed email, and names with `<`, `>` or control characters. It is available outside the cloud too, because gating it seemed unnecessary.
- **Root text:** the static root text and R-VCS now say commits use the configured git identity. The cloud steps appear only in `session-cloud-identity.md`, which the session-start hook injects when `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`. It sits after the core, before the state, and counts toward `CONTEXT_BUDGET`.
- **Gap:** a cloud session whose main thread is the root and which has no `.holyagent` and no legacy state gets no session-start context at all, so no identity steps. The `CloudAuthor` hint covers that case at commit time. I did not change this.
- **Not tested:** the signature check on GitHub. I only confirmed locally that the committer stays Claude and the author is the user.
- **For the root:** `/home/user/holyagent-identity/AGENTS.md` still says "`holyagent vcs` has two commands". It is outside my ownership paths, so I left it.
